entries: Patient assessment｜Respiratory symptoms and physician order checking｜Ask about respiratory symptoms, check history and physician orders, and obtain pulmonary function or blood gas data as authorized; record baseline, unknowns, and anomalies requiring physician judgment.

Treatment delivery｜Deliver respiratory therapy per orders｜Carry out authorized oxygen therapy, nebulization, airway clearance, or mechanical ventilation support per orders and organizational procedures; record the method, time, and patient response, and ask first before any adjustment beyond authority.

Continuous monitoring｜Observe patient and equipment response｜Monitor treatment response using vital signs, blood gases, respiratory effort, and equipment alarms; notify the clinical team immediately of changes and do not diagnose from a single reading.

Equipment safety｜Check and maintain equipment status｜Assemble, inspect, and clean respiratory equipment before treatment; when a fault is found, take it out of service and report it per procedure, keeping inspection, notification, and handover records.

Patient education｜Explain treatment and equipment use｜Within the team plan, explain treatment, breathing training, and home equipment use to patients and confirm their understanding; refer and record matters that cannot be completed alone.

Team handover｜Hand over accurately with the clinical team｜Check physician orders, treatment response, equipment status, and open risks with physicians, nurses, and the next shift; record escalations, the person taking over, and items pending review.

values: Materials and setup｜a completely fictional ward handover tabletop exercise

You are a respiratory therapy trainee and may only read fictional material, identify risks, and report to your clinical mentor; A1—A5 is not a physician order, and real patients must not be managed on that basis.

A1｜handover card: an adult patient coded P-01 is receiving physician-ordered respiratory support; the mentor requires checking patient identity, written physician orders, the previous record, and equipment status. The card provides no real treatment parameters.
A2｜the equipment log shows one alarm; the alarm time was recorded, but it does not say whether it persisted, what the patient's status was at the time, or who had taken over.

A3｜a monitoring record suggests one indicator deviates from this patient's physician order target; nearby there is also a verbal statement that the patient looks stable, which has not been verified by clinical personnel.
A4｜a nursing colleague says the on-duty physician was notified, but the handover form has no receipt time or follow-up instruction; the equipment checker has not signed either.

A5｜fictional organizational rules: trainees may only check original records, repeat risks to the mentor, and write de-identified handover drafts; patient assessment, treatment adjustment, and emergency handling are carried out by authorized clinical personnel under the real protocols.
Task and outputs

Using A1—A5, write a one-page handover checklist: list known records, unverified statements, equipment alarms, changes in patient status, physician orders, and notification receipts separately; flag the items requiring immediate judgment by the mentor and clinical team.

Then write an escalation draft containing no identity information, noting the alarm time, patient status pending verification, notification recipients, takeover confirmation, and follow-up review; do not write treatment parameters, diagnoses, or your own handling steps.
Reference approach (complete it independently first)

A1 checks whether patient identity, physician orders, and equipment records correspond to one another; A2 cannot be interpreted directly as an equipment fault or patient deterioration from one alarm, and authorized personnel should immediately check the site and the patient.

The monitoring anomaly in A3 and the claim of looking stable cannot cancel each other out; the source of the value, its time, and the unverified situation must be explained to the mentor and assessed by clinical personnel; the trainee does not adjust treatment alone.

The “notified” entry in A4 lacks a receipt and instruction, so at handover the recipient, time, person taking over, incomplete checks, and next review should be listed. A5 determines the permission boundary: simulated records keep the facts, unknowns, and action chain and contain no real patient information or any treatment settings.

Use fictional material only; do not infer diseases, provide oxygen flow or ventilator parameters, or train invasive procedures. Real patient anomalies must be handled by the authorized team per the organization's protocols; a tabletop work product is not proof of clinical ability or practice qualifications.

entries.answer: Respiratory therapists work with patients who have breathing difficulty or heart and lung problems. They first check patient identity, symptoms, and physician orders, then carry out oxygen therapy, nebulization, airway clearance, or mechanical ventilation-related tasks within their qualifications and organizational authorization. The work also includes equipment checks, continuous observation of response, recording treatment, and handing over to physicians and nurses. BLS and O*NET describe US occupational tasks; the specific tests, treatment parameters, and emergency handling are determined by local rules, physician orders, and organizational procedures.
entries.question: What do respiratory therapists do every day?

entries.answer: Existing evidence does not support the conclusion that AI will wholly replace respiratory therapists. Compliant tools may help with de-identified documentation, information retrieval, or to-do reminders, but on-site clinical assessment, equipment alarm judgment, treatment adjustment, and emergency escalation still require authorized personnel. Original physician orders, monitoring, and equipment records should be checked, and the source, omissions, and reviewer of generated content noted. ILO task exposure research discusses the range of tasks that may be affected, not hospital adoption rates or layoff forecasts for this occupation.
entries.question: Can AI replace respiratory therapists?

entries.answer: When a real patient or ventilator alarm occurs, follow the organization's patient safety and emergency protocols first and call the authorized clinical team for help. Handover should keep the observation time, original alarm or monitoring record, relevant physician orders, notification recipients, and takeover confirmation; not yet notified alone cannot be treated as the risk being resolved. Different equipment, patients, and situations require different actions, and a web page cannot provide safe on-site parameters or treatment steps. A1—A5 is only a fictional tabletop exercise and cannot replace clinical training or physician orders.
entries.question: What should be done when a ventilator alarm occurs?

entries.answer: China's 2022 occupational classification material lists respiratory therapist, code 4-14-01-04, so it can be confirmed that the occupational name exists in the Chinese classification. However, occupational classification, skill level, health professional qualification, and specific clinical authorization within a medical institution are different questions; a name alone or a US O*NET code does not mean independent diagnosis and treatment is permitted. When job seeking, check local policy, the target organization's announcements, supervisory relationships, equipment training, and onboarding assessment, and confirm the position's task boundaries with the organization if necessary.
entries.question: Does the occupation of respiratory therapist exist in China?

entries.answer:
This page has not yet obtained a precise national occupational wage distribution for respiratory therapists in mainland China. The 2025 National Bureau of Statistics pre-tax annual average wage for health and social work is 146,266 yuan for urban non-private units and 75,631 yuan for private units; above-scale enterprises in that industry, professional and technical personnel, is 110,500 yuan. These industry and broad job references cover different populations, are not this occupation's wage, median, or starting pay, and cannot be pieced into an income range or attributed to AI. Patient assessment, treatment 
delivery, and equipment monitoring correspond to the medical institution scenario. Above-scale enterprise professional and technical personnel is a broader and different survey population and does not represent public hospital respiratory therapists. Specific quotes must be checked by city, duties, hours, contract term, base pay and allowances/commission, and pre- or post-tax.
entries.question: What is the national wage for respiratory therapists in China?

entries.answer:
The May 2025 US respiratory therapist median annual wage published by BLS is 82,280 USD; the wage percentiles displayed by O*NET can be used to understand the national salaried employee distribution. The median is the midpoint of the distribution, not a new graduate starting wage, an individual contract amount, or a Chinese position quote. Industry medians also differ across hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, and physicians' offices; personal hours, region, employer, and shifts still affect actual income. When checking a target position, ask separately about pay 
composition and the pre- or post-tax basis.
entries.question: What is the median wage for respiratory therapists in the United States?

entries.answer: According to the BLS occupational outlook, the United States usually requires an accredited respiratory therapy associate program, with some employers preferring a bachelor's degree; the program includes anatomy, physiology, diagnosis, and treatment coursework plus supervised clinical practice. All states except Alaska require licensure, and specific application and continuing requirements must be checked by state. Certification, state licensure, and employer appointment also cannot substitute for one another. China has its own occupational classification and organizational requirements, and the US education and licensure path cannot be treated as a uniform Chinese threshold.
entries.question: How do you enter the respiratory therapy field in the United States?

entries.answer: Certification usually indicates passing an exam or standard of a professional organization; licensure is statutory access in the applicable jurisdiction; organizational authorization limits the specific position, equipment, patient population, and operations. Even with a certificate, a person may not satisfy local licensure and an employer's authorization for a particular treatment. US state rules differ, and Chinese positions also require checking the applicable system. In interviews, ask separately about the certifying body, legal requirements, pre-employment training, supervisors, and tasks that must not be performed alone.
entries.question: What is the difference between certification, licensure, and organizational authorization?

entries.answer: First check whether the target organization serves adults, children, or critical care patients, and in which scenarios such as emergency, wards, or home care; then check education, qualifications, the physician order chain, mentors, and organizational authorization. Working conditions also include respiratory equipment training, infection protection, physical load, night or holiday schedules, and the emergency help and handover mechanisms when patients deteriorate or equipment alarms. Pay requires checking hours, allowances, and the pre- or post-tax basis; fictional work can show thinking only and cannot prove clinical competence.
entries.question: What risks and conditions should be checked before entering the field?

entries.answer:
BLS expects US respiratory therapist employment to grow about 9% in 2025—2035, with about 8,600 job openings per year on average, including replacement demand from people changing jobs or leaving. This is a national projection and does not guarantee hiring opportunities in a region, hospital, or for an individual. Although physical therapists, nurses, and radiation therapists are also in medical settings, their service goals, education, licensure, and organizational authorization differ; those considering a transfer should check the target occupation's requirements item by item rather than automatically converting respiratory therapy experience into another occupational qualification
.
